indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.1.2.1 Recognise materials as important resources for providing human needs
indicator.objective: Investigate the uses of metals in everyday life and link the uses to their properties

skills.description: Identify everyday objects made from metals (e.g. farm tools, jewellery, cars, bridges, spoons).
Explain why a metal is used for a particular purpose because of its property (e.g. copper for wires because it conducts electricity; aluminium for roofing sheets because it is malleable).
Match a metal property to a correct everyday use.
Compare why different metals are used for different purposes.
Give examples of metals used in the home, school and community and state their uses.
Explain simply why metals are important in everyday life.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Any metal can be used for any purpose.
Metals are only used for jewellery.
Copper is used for wires because it is shiny.
Aluminium is used for roofing because it is heavy.
Metals have no link between their properties and uses.
Plastic is better than metal for all uses.

questions.stem: Which of these objects is made from metal?
hints: Which one is shiny and hard?
questions.explanation: A metal nail is made from metal. It is shiny, hard and strong.
questions.misconception: Metals are only used for jewellery.

questions.stem: Which of these farm tools is made from metal?
hints: Which part is hard and shiny?
questions.explanation: A cutlass blade is made from metal. It needs to be strong and sharp for cutting.
questions.misconception: Farm tools are only made of wood.

questions.stem: Name two objects in your home that are made from metal.
questions.explanation: Common metal objects at home include spoons, cooking pots, knives, door handles and nails.
questions.misconception: Metals are only used for jewellery.

questions.stem: Why is copper used to make electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper is used for electrical wires because it conducts electricity.
questions.misconception: Copper is used for wires because it is shiny.

questions.stem: Why is aluminium used to make roofing sheets?
options: Because it is malleable and can be pressed into thin sheets
Because it is ductile and can be drawn into wires
hints: Roofing sheets are thin and flat.
Aluminium can be pressed into sheets.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is malleable, so it can be pressed into thin sheets for roofing.
questions.misconception: Aluminium is used for roofing because it is heavy.

questions.stem: Why is copper used for electrical wires?
answer: it is a good conductor of electricity
questions.explanation: Copper is used for electrical wires because it conducts electricity.
questions.misconception: Copper is used for wires because it is shiny.

questions.stem: Why are cooking pots made from metals like aluminium?
hints: Pots need to get hot on the fire.
questions.explanation: Cooking pots are made from metals because metals conduct heat well, allowing food to cook evenly.
questions.misconception: Pots are made of metal because they are shiny.

questions.stem: Why is aluminium used for making cooking pots?
answer: aluminium is a good conductor of heat
it allows heat to pass through for cooking
questions.explanation: Aluminium is used for cooking pots because it is a good conductor of heat, allowing food to cook evenly.
questions.misconception: Pots are made of aluminium because it is shiny.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches a metal property to its use?
hints: Wires are made by drawing metal.
questions.explanation: Ductility allows metals to be drawn into wires, so it is linked to electrical wires.
questions.misconception: Lustre is used for cooking pots.

questions.stem: Which property of metals makes them suitable for making jewellery?
questions.explanation: Lustre (shininess) makes metals suitable for jewellery.
questions.misconception: Jewellery is made of metals because they are ductile.

questions.stem: Match the property to its use: ductility, malleability, conductivity.
answer: ductility - wires; malleability - sheets; conductivity - electrical wires or cooking pots
ductility: wires, malleability: sheets, conductivity: electrical wires
ductility for wires, malleability for sheets, conductivity for electrical wires and pots
questions.explanation: Ductility is used for wires, malleability for sheets, and conductivity for electrical wires and cooking pots.
questions.misconception: All metal properties have the same use.

questions.stem: Which of these correctly links a metal property to an everyday object?
questions.explanation: Lustre (shininess) is linked to jewellery. Ductility is for wires, malleability is for sheets, and conductivity is for wires and pots.
questions.misconception: Ductility is for roofing sheets.

questions.stem: Why is copper used for electrical wires while aluminium is used for roofing sheets?
options: Copper conducts electricity; aluminium is malleable for sheets
Copper is malleable; aluminium conducts electricity
Both are used for the same reason
Copper is shiny; aluminium is heavy
hints: Each metal is used for a different property.
Copper conducts electricity; aluminium can be pressed into sheets.
questions.explanation: Copper is used for wires because it conducts electricity. Aluminium is used for roofing sheets because it is malleable and can be pressed into thin sheets.
questions.misconception: All metals are used for the same reason.

questions.stem: Compare why copper is used for wires and aluminium is used for cooking pots.
answer: copper conducts electricity for wires, while aluminium conducts heat for cooking pots
copper is used for wires because it conducts electricity; aluminium is used for pots because it conducts heat
copper: electrical conductivity; aluminium: heat conductivity
hints: Think about what wires and pots need to do.
Both need conductivity, but of different types.
questions.explanation: Copper is used for wires because it conducts electricity. Aluminium is used for cooking pots because it conducts heat well.
questions.misconception: All metals are used for the same purpose.

questions.stem: Two metals are available for making a cooking pot and an electrical wire. Metal A conducts heat well and is malleable. Metal B conducts electricity well and is ductile. Which metal is better for each use?
options: Metal A for pots, Metal B for wires
Metal A for wires, Metal B for pots
hints: Wires need electrical conduction and ductility.
questions.explanation: Metal A is better for cooking pots because it conducts heat and is malleable. Metal B is better for wires because it conducts electricity and is ductile.
questions.misconception: Any metal is suitable for any purpose.

questions.stem: Which metal object is used at school?
hints: Which one is made of metal?
questions.explanation: A metal scissors is used at school for cutting paper.
questions.misconception: Metals are not used at school.

questions.stem: Give two examples of metals used in the community and state their uses.
answer: metal roofs for buildings, metal tools for farming
aluminium for roofing, iron for tools
copper for wires, iron for bridges
questions.explanation: Metals are used in the community for roofs (aluminium), tools (iron), bridges (steel), and electrical wires (copper).
questions.misconception: Metals have no community uses.

questions.stem: A bridge is built using steel. Which property makes steel suitable for this use?
questions.explanation: Steel is used for bridges because it is strong and hard, allowing it to support heavy loads.
questions.misconception: Bridges are built with soft metals.

questions.stem: Why are metals important in everyday life?
options: They are used to make tools, utensils and buildings
They are only used for decoration
They are only found in labs
hints: Think about cooking utensils and tools.
questions.explanation: Metals are important because they are used to make tools, utensils, buildings, wires and many other things we use daily.
questions.misconception: Metals are only for decoration.

questions.stem: Write a short paragraph (3–4 sentences) explaining why metals are important in everyday life. Include at least two examples and one property linked to a use.

criteria.description: Stated that metals are important for making tools/utensils/buildings
Gave at least two correct examples of metal uses
Linked one metal property to a specific use

hints: Think about cooking pots, wires, or tools.
Link a property like conductivity to wires.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Metals are not important.
